This paper proposes a novel method for enhancing reinforcement learning by leveraging high-reward experiences to reshape reward signals. The authors aim to address the common issues of sparse rewards and lack of behavioral diversity in complex environments. The core contribution is a mechanism that prioritizes high-performing trajectories to guide the agent toward optimal policies more efficiently. The theoretical foundation of the approach is sound and well-supported by existing literature on reward shaping. The experimental design is comprehensive, covering several benchmark environments to demonstrate the method's generalizability. I found the results section particularly convincing, as the proposed method consistently outperforms standard PPO and SAC baselines. The increase in behavioral diversity is clearly evidenced by the state-space coverage plots. However, the paper would benefit from a more detailed explanation of the hyperparameters used for reward scaling. It is unclear how sensitive the algorithm is to the specific weight assigned to the high-reward experience buffer. The authors should include an ablation study to isolate the impact of the shaping signal from the experience replay mechanism. Additionally, the computational overhead of maintaining the high-reward buffer is not fully discussed. Providing a time-to-convergence comparison would help readers understand the trade-off between sample efficiency and wall-clock time. Some of the figures are slightly cluttered and would benefit from larger axis labels for better readability. The related work section is thorough, though a more recent discussion on intrinsic motivation methods would strengthen the context. The writing is generally clear, but there are a few typographical errors in the methodology section. Specifically, the notation for the modified reward function is inconsistent between equation three and equation five. I suggest the authors clarify the mathematical definition of the shaping term to avoid ambiguity. Despite these minor concerns, the technical contribution is significant and provides a practical solution to a persistent RL problem. The method's ability to prevent premature convergence to local optima is a highlight of the work. I believe this research will be of high interest to the community focusing on robotic control and game AI. Once the requested clarifications and minor edits are made, the paper will be a strong addition to the field. I recommend the paper for acceptance with minor revisions. The findings provide a promising direction for future research into adaptive reward systems. Overall, the work is a well-executed study with impressive empirical results.

Title: Effects of Blackcurrant Supplementation on Muscle Force, Fatigue, and Recovery Across Different Muscle Fiber Profiles

Abstract
This study investigated the impact of blackcurrant supplementation on muscular performance and recovery in individuals with varying muscle fiber compositions. Anthocyanins found in blackcurrants are hypothesized to reduce oxidative stress and inflammation. We measured peak force, time to fatigue, and recovery rates in participants categorized by slow-twitch and fast-twitch dominance. Results indicate that blackcurrant supplementation significantly improves recovery time and reduces fatigue markers, particularly in fast-twitch dominant individuals. These findings suggest that polyphenol-rich diets may optimize athletic performance based on genetic fiber profiles.

Introduction
Skeletal muscle performance is governed by a complex interplay of metabolic capacity and structural composition. Muscle fibers are generally categorized into Type I slow-twitch and Type II fast-twitch fibers. Type I fibers are oxidative and fatigue-resistant, whereas Type II fibers are glycolytic and generate high force but fatigue quickly. Exercise-induced muscle damage often leads to delayed onset muscle soreness and a temporary decrease in force production. Oxidative stress plays a central role in this degradation process. Blackcurrants are rich in anthocyanins, which possess potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Previous research suggests that these compounds can mitigate muscle damage. However, it remains unclear if these benefits vary according to muscle fiber profile. Understanding this interaction is crucial for personalized sports nutrition. This paper aims to fill that gap by examining specific effects on force and fatigue. We hypothesize that fast-twitch fibers, being more prone to oxidative damage, will show greater improvement.

Methods
A double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted with forty healthy adults. Participants were screened for their muscle fiber profile using biopsy and ultrasound analysis. Twenty participants were categorized as Type I dominant, and twenty as Type II dominant. Participants were randomly assigned to either a blackcurrant juice group or a placebo group. The supplementation period lasted four weeks, with a daily dose of 150 milliliters of concentrated juice. Baseline muscle force was measured using an isometric dynamometer. Fatigue was assessed through a sustained maximal voluntary contraction test. Recovery was monitored via creatine kinase levels and subjective soreness scales over seventy-two hours. All exercises were standardized to ensure consistency across the cohort. Dietary intake was controlled to prevent confounding effects from other antioxidants. Statistical analysis was performed using a two-way ANOVA to determine interaction effects between supplementation and fiber type. Significance was set at p less than 0.05.

Results
Peak force production at baseline showed no significant difference between the supplement and placebo groups. However, during the fatigue tests, the blackcurrant group exhibited a slower decline in force. This effect was more pronounced in the Type II dominant group compared to the Type I group. Specifically, fast-twitch dominant individuals showed a twelve percent increase in time to exhaustion. Recovery markers revealed a significant reduction in serum creatine kinase in the supplement group. The Type II dominant group experienced a faster return to baseline force levels within forty-eight hours. In contrast, the Type I dominant group showed modest improvements in recovery time. Subjective soreness reports were lower in the blackcurrant group across both fiber profiles. The interaction between fiber type and supplementation was statistically significant for recovery rate. These data suggest a synergistic effect between anthocyanins and glycolytic muscle metabolism.

Discussion
The results support the hypothesis that blackcurrant supplementation enhances muscle recovery and fatigue resistance. The disparity between fiber types can be explained by metabolic differences. Fast-twitch fibers rely more on anaerobic glycolysis, which can lead to rapid accumulation of metabolites. The antioxidant properties of blackcurrants likely neutralize reactive oxygen species more effectively in these high-stress environments. Type I fibers, being naturally more oxidative, may already possess higher endogenous antioxidant levels. This would explain the smaller relative improvement observed in slow-twitch dominant participants. The reduction in creatine kinase indicates a preservation of sarcolemma integrity. This protection allows for a quicker return to peak power output after exhaustive exercise. These findings have implications for athletes specializing in power sports. Sprinters and weightlifters, who possess more Type II fibers, may benefit most from anthocyanin supplementation. Conversely, endurance athletes may see smaller but still meaningful gains. The timing of supplementation also appears critical for maximizing the anti-inflammatory window.

Conclusion
Blackcurrant supplementation effectively reduces muscle fatigue and accelerates recovery. The magnitude of these effects is dependent on the individual's muscle fiber profile. Fast-twitch dominant individuals derive the greatest benefit in terms of force maintenance and recovery speed. This study highlights the importance of tailoring nutritional interventions to physiological characteristics. Future research should explore the long-term effects of various polyphenol dosages. Additionally, investigating the molecular pathways of anthocyanin interaction with myosin heavy chains would be beneficial. Overall, blackcurrants serve as a viable natural supplement for enhancing muscular resilience. This approach offers a safe strategy to optimize athletic performance across diverse populations. Further clinical trials are warranted to confirm these results in elite athletes. Consistent intake of anthocyanins may provide a competitive edge in high-intensity sports.

The submitted paper presents a novel approach to high-resolution autoregressive image generation by introducing multiscale pixel ordering and progressive color-bit modeling. The authors address a critical bottleneck in autoregressive models which is the computational cost and sequential nature of pixel-by-pixel prediction. The proposed multiscale strategy allows the model to capture global structures before refining local details. This hierarchical approach is a logical extension of existing image pyramids and shows promise in improving coherence. The progressive color-bit modeling is particularly interesting as it decomposes the color space into a sequence of bit-planes. By predicting the most significant bits first, the model can establish the general color tone before refining the precision. This technique effectively reduces the vocabulary size for each prediction step, which should lead to faster convergence. The mathematical formulation of the probability distribution over bit-planes is clear and well-supported. The experimental results demonstrate a measurable improvement in Fréchet Inception Distance compared to baseline autoregressive models. The visual quality of the generated images is impressive, especially regarding edge sharpness and structural integrity. I appreciate the thorough ablation study that isolates the contributions of multiscale ordering and bit modeling. However, there are several areas where the manuscript requires further clarification and improvement. The complexity analysis of the multiscale ordering is somewhat superficial and needs more detail. Specifically, the authors should provide a formal big-O notation for the inference time per image. The comparison with latent diffusion models is missing, which is a significant omission given the current state of the art. While autoregressive models have their own strengths, a direct comparison with diffusion-based methods would provide necessary context. The author's claim regarding memory efficiency is not fully substantiated by the provided data. I suggest including a table that lists peak VRAM usage during both training and inference. The choice of the specific multiscale ordering pattern seems heuristic; a more rigorous justification for this choice is needed. It would be beneficial to see if other ordering strategies, such as Z-order curves, yield similar results. The paper also lacks a discussion on the impact of different bit-depths on the final image quality. Does the model struggle when moving from 8-bit to 16-bit color representations? The related works section is comprehensive but fails to mention several recent papers on variable-rate image coding. Integrating these references would strengthen the theoretical grounding of the progressive bit modeling. Some of the figures are too small to clearly see the artifacts in the generated images. I recommend providing high-resolution zoomed-in patches to highlight the benefits of the progressive refinement. The writing is generally clear, although there are several typographical errors in the third section. The transition between the multiscale discussion and the bit-modeling section is somewhat abrupt. A bridging paragraph explaining the synergy between the two methods would improve the flow. The hyperparameters used for the Transformer backbone are listed, but the learning rate schedule is not fully described. For reproducibility, the authors must include the specific optimizer settings and weight decay values. The evaluation metrics are standard, but including a user study for perceptual quality would add significant value. Quantitative metrics often fail to capture the nuance of structural distortions in high-resolution images. The authors should also discuss the limitations of the autoregressive nature, specifically the potential for error accumulation. Does the multiscale approach mitigate the drift that typically occurs in long sequences? The analysis of the loss curves is basic and would benefit from a discussion on gradient stability. I am curious if the model exhibits any mode collapse during the training of the lower-bit planes. The conclusion is a bit generic and should more explicitly state the broader implications for generative modeling. Future work could explore the application of this method to video generation or 3D voxels. Despite these concerns, the technical contribution is solid and the results are encouraging. The combination of spatial and color-space decomposition is a clever way to handle high-dimensional data. If the authors address the missing comparisons and provide more detailed complexity analysis, the paper will be much stronger. I believe this work provides a valuable contribution to the field of image synthesis. The novelty of the bit-plane approach is a highlight of the research. Overall, the paper is a strong candidate for publication pending the suggested revisions. I recommend a major revision to address the gaps in evaluation and theoretical justification. The potential for this architecture to scale to even higher resolutions is an exciting prospect. I look forward to seeing the revised version of this promising work.

Facial-expression technology offers a novel way for educators to monitor student engagement and emotional states in real time. By analyzing micro-expressions, this technology can alert teachers when students are confused or bored, allowing for immediate instructional adjustments. Such data-driven insights can help personalize learning experiences to better meet the emotional needs of each student. However, these systems face significant limitations regarding accuracy and cultural nuance. Facial expressions are not universal, and a neutral face does not always indicate a lack of interest. There are also serious privacy concerns regarding the collection and storage of biometric data from minors. Relying solely on algorithms may lead to misinterpretations of a student's internal state. Furthermore, the presence of surveillance cameras can create an environment of anxiety that hinders genuine learning. Ultimately, while these tools provide useful data, they should supplement rather than replace human intuition. A balanced approach ensures that technology supports the teacher-student relationship without compromising privacy or emotional authenticity.

Completing all four years of high school is a vital milestone that provides students with essential academic and social advantages. While some may feel the urge to accelerate their education, staying the full course ensures a comprehensive learning experience. Academically, the final two years often contain the most rigorous and specialized courses. These advanced classes prepare students for the intensity of college-level work and critical thinking. Without these years, a student might miss out on key prerequisites for higher education. Beyond academics, high school serves as a critical period for emotional and social maturation. Students learn how to navigate complex peer relationships and develop necessary conflict-resolution skills. These soft skills are just as important as textbook knowledge in the professional world. Furthermore, the full four-year experience allows students to explore various extracurricular activities. Whether through sports, music, or clubs, these activities help students discover their passions and interests. Building a strong portfolio of achievements over four years makes a candidate more competitive for scholarships. It also provides more time to build meaningful mentorships with teachers and counselors. These adults often provide the guidance and recommendation letters needed for future success. Additionally, completing the full term instills a sense of discipline and perseverance. Finishing what one started creates a psychological foundation of achievement and resilience. Entering the workforce or college prematurely can lead to a lack of confidence compared to peers. Ultimately, the four-year journey transforms a teenager into a well-rounded young adult. By investing the full time, students secure a more stable and promising future.

The debate between homeschooling and traditional in-person schooling involves a complex trade-off between academic customization and social integration. One of the primary academic advantages of homeschooling is the ability to provide a personalized curriculum tailored to a student's specific strengths and weaknesses. Students can progress through material at their own pace, allowing them to master difficult concepts without the pressure of a classroom schedule. Furthermore, one-on-one instruction often leads to higher efficiency and a more profound engagement with the subject matter. In contrast, traditional schools often follow a rigid pace that may leave some students behind or bore those who are advanced. However, these academic gains often come at a significant social cost. Attending school in person provides a natural environment for children to develop essential interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence. In a traditional classroom, students learn how to navigate peer conflicts, collaborate in diverse groups, and build lasting friendships. Homeschooled children may struggle with social isolation if their parents do not proactively seek out community groups or extracurricular activities. The lack of daily interaction with a wide variety of personalities can hinder a child's ability to adapt to unfamiliar social settings. Moreover, the school environment teaches students how to function within a larger institutional hierarchy. While homeschooling offers an intellectual sanctuary, it may lack the spontaneous social challenges that build resilience. Ultimately, the choice depends on whether a family prioritizes academic precision or a broad social experience. Both methods have the potential to produce successful adults if their respective shortcomings are managed. Balancing rigorous study with intentional social exposure remains the key to a comprehensive education.

The United States Electoral College is an outdated system that no longer serves the needs of a modern democracy. The most fundamental principle of a fair election is that every single vote should carry equal weight. Under the current system, however, a vote in a small swing state often holds more influence than a vote in a large, non-competitive state. This disparity encourages candidates to ignore the vast majority of the country to focus on a few key battlegrounds. Millions of voters are effectively disenfranchised when their preferred candidate wins their state by a narrow margin, causing their vote to disappear. Furthermore, the Electoral College allows for the possibility that a candidate can win the presidency without receiving the most individual votes nationwide. This outcome contradicts the basic democratic idea that the person with the most support should lead the country. A transition to a nationwide popular vote would ensure that the will of the people is directly reflected in the final result. It would motivate candidates to campaign in every state, reaching out to diverse populations regardless of their geography. Voters in "safe" states would feel more empowered to participate, knowing their choice truly matters. The current system creates a risk of faithless electors, who can theoretically vote against their state's population. Removing this layer of mediation would eliminate unnecessary unpredictability and potential corruption. Opponents argue that the current system protects small states, but this is a misconception. In reality, it only protects a handful of swing states while ignoring the rural needs of others. A popular vote treats every citizen as an equal stakeholder in the government. It simplifies the process and makes the outcome easier for the general public to understand. Such a change would modernize American politics and strengthen the legitimacy of the executive branch. Ultimately, the presidency represents the entire nation, not just a collection of state interests. It is time to embrace a system that is truly representative of the American people. Adopting a direct popular vote is the only way to guarantee true democratic fairness.

Beyond the traditional confines of the classroom, extracurricular activities provide a vital arena for holistic student development. While academic achievement is often the primary focus of schooling, engagement in clubs, sports, and the arts is equally essential. These activities serve as a bridge between theoretical learning and practical life experience. First, extracurricular involvement significantly bolsters a student's overall well-being. Engaging in a passion project or a physical sport acts as a necessary release from the pressures of rigorous coursework. This diversion reduces stress and prevents the burnout often associated with high academic expectations. Physical activities, in particular, promote health and release endorphins that improve mood. Furthermore, the pursuit of a hobby provides a sense of accomplishment and purpose. When students master a new skill, their self-esteem grows. This internal confidence often translates back into the classroom, creating a positive feedback loop. In addition to mental health, these activities are the primary catalysts for social connection. Schools are large environments where it can be difficult to find like-minded peers. Joining a specific club allows students to meet others who share their niche interests. These shared goals foster a sense of belonging and community. Through teamwork in sports or collaboration in theater, students learn the nuances of interpersonal communication. They experience the challenges of conflict resolution and the rewards of mutual support. These bonds often form the foundation of lifelong friendships. Social integration reduces feelings of isolation and loneliness among the youth. Moreover, the diverse nature of extracurriculars exposes students to different perspectives and backgrounds. This interaction cultivates empathy and cultural competence. Personal growth is the ultimate byproduct of these combined social and emotional benefits. Participation in these activities requires discipline, time management, and dedication. A student must learn to balance practice schedules with homework deadlines. This teaches them how to prioritize tasks and handle responsibility independently. Leadership opportunities often arise within these groups, allowing students to guide others toward a common goal. Taking initiative in a club setting builds decision-making skills and resilience. When a team loses or a performance fails, students learn how to cope with disappointment. They discover that failure is not a dead end but a stepping stone toward improvement. This growth mindset is critical for success in adulthood. Furthermore, exploring various activities helps students discover their true passions and strengths. A student might discover a talent for debate or a love for coding that they never encountered in a textbook. This self-discovery informs future career choices and educational paths. By stepping outside their comfort zone, students expand their identity. They become well-rounded individuals rather than just academic performers. Ultimately, the integration of extracurriculars creates a balanced educational experience. It ensures that the mind, body, and spirit are nurtured simultaneously. Education should be about more than just passing tests. It should be about preparing a human being for the complexities of the real world. Therefore, schools must continue to value and fund these diverse programs. When students are encouraged to explore, they thrive in every aspect of their lives. Extracurricular involvement is not a distraction from learning but a fundamental part of it. It equips students with the emotional intelligence and social skills needed for a fulfilling life. In conclusion, the benefits of these activities are indispensable for a healthy transition to adulthood.

Abstract. This study examines the price transmission dynamics among corn producers, wholesalers, and retailers in Tuban Regency. Using a Vector Error Correction Model, the research analyzes both short-term fluctuations and long-term equilibrium relationships. Results indicate a significant long-term cointegration among the three tiers of the marketing chain. However, short-term price adjustments are asymmetrical, with retail prices rising faster than producer prices. These findings suggest an imbalance in bargaining power within the local supply chain.

Introduction. Corn is a strategic commodity for food security and livestock feed in Tuban Regency. The pricing mechanism for corn involves multiple intermediaries, which can affect the income of smallholder farmers. Understanding how price changes move from the farm gate to the consumer is essential for policy interventions. Price transmission describes the process by which price changes in one market are passed on to another. Efficient markets typically exhibit symmetric and rapid price transmission. In many developing regions, market imperfections lead to inefficient transmission. Such inefficiencies often result in producers receiving a smaller share of the final retail price. This paper focuses on the specific spatial and institutional context of Tuban Regency. The objective is to determine if prices are integrated across the production, wholesale, and retail levels.

Literature Review. Previous studies on agricultural price transmission highlight the role of market power. Asymmetric price transmission often occurs when wholesalers or retailers possess dominant market positions. The Vector Error Correction Model is widely regarded as the standard tool for analyzing these dynamics. Cointegration tests allow researchers to identify long-term stable relationships despite short-term volatility. In Indonesia, corn markets are often characterized by fragmented production and centralized distribution. Previous research in East Java suggests that infrastructure gaps can hinder price synchronization. Transaction costs play a significant role in the margins captured by intermediaries. Understanding these margins helps in identifying where bottlenecks exist in the value chain. The theory of efficient markets suggests that prices should adjust instantaneously to new information. However, behavioral factors and storage capacities often create lags.

Methodology. The data used in this study consists of monthly average prices from 2020 to 2025. Prices were collected from the Tuban Regency Department of Agriculture and local market surveys. The dataset includes producer prices, wholesale prices, and retail prices. To ensure stationarity, the Augmented Dickey-Fuller test was applied to all price series. Most series were found to be non-stationary at levels but stationary at first differences. The Johansen Cointegration Test was used to determine the existence of a long-term relationship. After confirming cointegration, a Vector Error Correction Model was developed. This model separates the short-term dynamics from the long-term equilibrium. The Error Correction Term indicates the speed at which the system returns to equilibrium after a shock. Impulse response functions were used to visualize the reaction of one price to a shock in another. Variance decomposition was employed to determine the proportion of price volatility explained by each actor.

Results and Discussion. The Johansen test revealed one cointegrating vector among the three price series. This confirms that producer, wholesale, and retail prices move together over the long term. The long-term relationship is positive and statistically significant. A rise in producer prices eventually leads to a rise in retail prices. However, the short-term results show a distinct pattern of asymmetry. When producer prices increase, wholesale and retail prices respond rapidly. Conversely, when producer prices decrease, the retail price declines much more slowly. This suggests that retailers are able to maintain higher prices even when input costs drop. The Error Correction Term shows a moderate adjustment speed of approximately twenty percent per month. This means it takes several months for a price shock to be fully absorbed. The impulse response analysis indicates that wholesale prices are the primary driver of retail fluctuations. Producer prices have a delayed but significant impact on wholesale levels. This lag is likely due to the storage capacity of wholesalers who can buffer price swings. The marketing margin is highest at the retail level, followed by the wholesale level. Producers receive the lowest proportion of the final consumer price. This disparity highlights the vulnerability of corn farmers in Tuban Regency. Factors such as lack of storage and limited market information exacerbate this issue. Producers are often forced to sell immediately after harvest when prices are lowest. Wholesalers leverage this timing to secure lower purchase prices.

Conclusion. The price relationship among corn actors in Tuban Regency is characterized by long-term integration but short-term inefficiency. The asymmetrical transmission of prices favors the downstream actors over the upstream producers. This suggests that the market is not perfectly competitive and is influenced by intermediaries. To improve farmer welfare, the local government should implement price stabilization programs. Strengthening farmer cooperatives could provide better bargaining power and storage options. Providing real-time market information to producers would reduce the information asymmetry. Improving infrastructure to reduce transport costs may also enhance price synchronization. Further research should explore the impact of seasonal variations on these price relationships. Understanding the role of government subsidies in price flooring is also recommended. In summary, while the prices are linked, the benefits of price increases do not flow equitably back to the farmers. Addressing these gaps is crucial for a sustainable agricultural economy in Tuban.
